hypotheses.cause_description: Unmetered air entering after the MAF sensor causes a lean condition. This is the most common cause of P0171 and is often free or cheap to fix.
supporting_evidence: P0171 with elevated LTFT strongly suggests vacuum leak
Rough idle further supports air leak diagnosis
Long-term fuel trim is +14.8% — elevated, indicating lean/rich condition
what_could_make_this_wrong: If LTFT is only slightly elevated, the cause may be a weak O2 sensor not a real lean condition
Confidence capped at 75% due to incomplete scan data — physical inspection needed to confirm

hypotheses.cause_description: A contaminated MAF sensor under-reports airflow, causing the ECU to run lean. MAF sensors are wear items on high-mileage vehicles.
supporting_evidence: Dirty MAF is a leading lean-code cause
MAF value below expected range for RPM supports this
Long-term fuel trim is +14.8% — elevated, indicating lean/rich condition
what_could_make_this_wrong: MAF cleaning with sensor-safe spray is a $5 first step — try this before replacement

hypotheses.cause_name: Weak Fuel Pump / Low Fuel Pressure
hypotheses.cause_description: Insufficient fuel pressure causes lean conditions, especially under load or at highway speeds.
supporting_evidence: Lean codes with load-based symptoms suggest fuel pressure issue
Long-term fuel trim is +14.8% — elevated, indicating lean/rich condition
what_could_make_this_wrong: Requires fuel pressure gauge test to confirm — cannot be confirmed from OBD-II data alone
